Fellow Eligibility Key Dates FAQ's Support the Commonwealth Startup Fellowship What is the Commonwealth Startup Fellowship? This six-month programme is designed to fuel high-potential startups through intensive in-person and online learning. You’ll gain essential skills, benefit from tailored coaching, and get access to a powerful global network to help you overcome barriers and scale up your business. The
The programme includes a fully funded two-week bootcamp in Accra, Ghana (January 2027), plus ongoing online support with business coaching, expert-led sessions, and valuable peer connections.

One founder from each selected team will participate in-person, while co-founders and team members can access the remote portion, connecting with global mentors and industry experts from across the Commonwealth.
In addition to training and mentorship, participating teams can apply for financial support through the Fellows Fund.
Each startup may apply for up to £2,000 as equity-free grant to cover business-related expenses and support the development and growth of their venture.
Select participants will be invited to a Capstone in London, UK (May 2027), where they will have the chance to pitch to investors and industry leaders.
Two-week in-person Bootcamp In person training – Accra, Ghana Workshops, covering topics such as leadership, scaling a business, building a team, fundraising and sales.
The Commonwealth Startup Fellowship is designed for startups that have already demonstrated market demand and are preparing for growth and expansion.
The Commonwealth Startup Fellowship is open to startups from all sectors and industries.

However founders building technology-enabled solutions or ventures that can benefit from access to scientific expertise, innovation ecosystems, research facilities, and global networks may find particular value in the Fellowship.

This is especially relevant for startups addressing challenges related to: Climate and sustainability Energy and clean technologies Health and wellbeing Advanced technologies and digital innovation Science-based and engineering-led solutions Who is this fellowship not for?
The programme is designed for growth-stage startups rather than ventures that are still validating their idea or have already reached significant international scale.

Finally, the Fellowship is not intended for charities, non-profit organisations, or ventures that rely primarily on donations, philanthropy, or grant funding rather than a sustainable revenue-generating business model.

That’s where EarthScale comes in. EarthScale is a UK-wide, 12-month programme designed to support climate tech ventures to scale, navigate manufacturing, and raise Series A funding. Imperial College London leads the programme through a collaboration between the Imperial Enterprise Lab and Undaunted . EarthScale brings together a growing collaborative network of university-led regional hubs, including Imperial College London, Cranfield University, the University of Derby, the University of Exeter, the University of Leeds and the University of Nottingham.

Championing diversity For founders of Black and mixed-Black heritage, the entrepreneurial journey can be especially challenging, facing multiple disparities such as access to capital. At Imperial Enterprise Lab, we believe that diversity is a competitive advantage not a tick box, b ut founders of Black and mixed-Black heritage face multiple barriers and limited support compared to their white counterparts. Extend VC reported that between 2009 and 2019 only 0.24% of venture capital raised in the UK went to Black founders, of which only 0.02% went to Black female founders. While there was a brief uptick in the tech sector, with Black founders receiving around 1.13% of UK tech venture funding in 2021, this progress was not sustained and their share fell back to approximately 0.95% by 2023, underlining that the funding gap remains stark.

We think great things can only happen when everyone has a seat at the table, which is why WE Innovate was created. For over 10 years, WE Innovate has inspired and empowered over 600 women-led startup founders who have gone on to raise £88 million collectively in funding. WE Innovate is a six-month, three-phase initiative which runs from January to June. Through expert-led masterclasses, personalised coaching, and mentoring , 25 women-led teams gain the entrepreneurial skills, confidence, and

Through expert-led masterclasses, personalised coaching, and mentoring , 25 women-led teams gain the entrepreneurial skills, confidence, and networks needed to transform early-stage ideas into pitch-ready startups.
The programme culminates in a pitch competition, where each finalist team competes for a share of a £30,000 equity-free prize fund.
You will also join a fast-growing support network of women founders from across the UK.
Your team lead must be a current undergraduate, post-graduate student or Early Career Researcher at Imperial College London OR must have graduated within the last 2 years.
In-person sessions typically take place at the Enterprise Lab at South Kensington Campus.
For sessions at the Enterprise Lab there is an access lift and an accessible bathroom on the studio level.
